title: Best spreadsheet-style BI tools for cloud data warehouses (2026): 9 options for teams that work in formulas, not SQL
summary: Sigma, Omni, Row Zero, and Excel on Power BI let ops and finance teams work in a grid on warehouse data. 9 tools compared on live queries, metrics, and price.
body_markdown:
The best spreadsheet-style BI tools for cloud data warehouses in November 2026 are Sigma, Omni, Row Zero, and Microsoft Excel connected to Power BI semantic models, with Google Sheets Connected Sheets, Coefficient, Quadratic, Equals, and Basedash covering narrower needs. Sigma and Omni pair a spreadsheet grid with governed metric definitions, so operations teams can pivot and write formulas while every department sees the same KPIs. Row Zero is the closest thing to real Excel on warehouse data, and Databricks acquired it in September 2026. Excel on Power BI is the default for Microsoft shops that already maintain semantic models.


The hard part is not the grid. It is keeping spreadsheet flexibility while stopping every analyst from defining revenue their own way.


## How we evaluated spreadsheet-style BI tools


We checked each vendor’s official pricing pages and documentation on November 19, 2026, against five criteria taken from the questions ops, finance, and data leaders ask when they shortlist these tools:


1. **Spreadsheet fidelity:** Excel-compatible formulas, pivot tables, and whether users can type values into cells or write them back to the warehouse.
2. **Query model:** live queries on every interaction, query results imported into the sheet, or scheduled syncs, and how often data refreshes.
3. **Governed metrics:** whether formulas and pivots can sit on shared, reviewed definitions (a semantic layer, data model, or metrics) instead of each user’s own logic.
4. **Security and audit:** per-user warehouse permissions or row-level security, SAML SSO, SCIM, and audit logs, which matter when leadership wants lineage and a record of who saw what.
5. **Price and AI:** a published starting price, the pricing model, and what the AI features actually do.

## Sigma: best for governed spreadsheet BI on Snowflake, Databricks, or BigQuery


**Best for:** data teams that want business users building their own pivots and formulas on live warehouse data, on top of definitions the data team controls. **Not ideal for:** finance models that depend on cell-by-cell references, or buyers who want a published price.


- **Pricing:** Sigma doesn’t publish prices; its pricing URL redirects to a contact form. Licenses come in[View, Act, Analyze, and Build tiers](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/account-type-and-license-overview) , and some actions use[billable credits](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/about-billable-usage-events) : input tables cost “1 input credit per row,” and agent messages cost 0.1 credit each from November 1, 2026. Sigma offers a[7-day free trial](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/start-your-sigma-trial) . Verified November 2026.
- **Spreadsheet features:** Sigma supports[over 200 functions](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/function-index) , pivot tables, and[input tables](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/intro-to-input-tables) that write typed values to a writeback schema on Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, PostgreSQL, or Redshift. Functions calculate over columns and groups rather than individual cell references, so Excel models built cell by cell need to be rebuilt as column logic.
- **Governed metrics:**[data models](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/get-started-with-data-modeling) “provide a semantic layer for your data,” and[metrics](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/about-metrics) are reusable calculations tied to a data source.
- **Security:**[row-level security](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/set-up-row-level-security) uses user attributes, team membership, or email. SAML 2.0 and OIDC are supported,[SCIM requires SAML](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/manage-users-and-teams-with-scim) , and the[audit log connection](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/enable-audit-logging) is off until an admin enables it.
- **AI:** Sigma Assistant answers natural-language questions, and the formula assistant writes, fixes, and explains formulas.
- **Tradeoff:** Sigma “does not store your data” and relies on browser and warehouse-level[caching](https://help.sigmacomputing.com/docs/caching-and-data-freshness) , so data stays current but heavy exploration adds warehouse compute.


## Omni: best when a dbt-based semantic model should drive the spreadsheet


**Best for:** teams with a dbt project and a data team that wants analysts to explore in Excel-style tabs without leaving the governed model. **Not ideal for:** finance users who want a standalone spreadsheet, or anyone who needs an Excel add-in today.


- **Pricing:** Omni doesn’t publish prices, and trials go through a[demo request](https://omni.co/demo) . AI features use credits, and usage beyond the included amount[requires overage billing](https://docs.omni.co/ai/settings/usage) . Verified November 2026.
- **Spreadsheet features:**[spreadsheet tabs](https://docs.omni.co/analyze-explore/spreadsheet-tabs) “bring the power of traditional Excel spreadsheets into your existing reporting and analysis workflows, with the added benefit of always-on, live data.” Omni says its[calculations](https://docs.omni.co/analyze-explore/calculations) aim “to be compatible with Excel or Google Sheets wherever possible.”[Input columns](https://docs.omni.co/analyze-explore/input-columns) write typed values to your connection’s scratch schema.
- **Governed metrics:** the[shared model](https://docs.omni.co/modeling/develop/promotion) “governs every workbook on the connection,” and analysts can promote workbook-level logic into it. The[dbt integration](https://docs.omni.co/integrations/dbt) works in both directions.
- **Query model:** Omni queries the warehouse directly, and[results are cached for 6 hours by default](https://docs.omni.co/analyze-explore/performance/caching) .
- **Security:**[access_filters](https://docs.omni.co/modeling/topics/parameters/access-filters) restrict rows by user attribute. Omni supports[SAML and OIDC](https://docs.omni.co/administration/authentication) , SCIM for Okta, Entra, and Rippling, and[audit logs](https://docs.omni.co/administration/audit-logs) delivered to S3, GCS, or Azure Blob.
- **AI:** the Omni Agent answers questions in chat, and the formula builder turns a plain-English description into “a working Excel-style formula” ([Omni AI](https://docs.omni.co/ai) ).
- **Tradeoff:** an Excel add-in has only been shown as a demo, and Google Sheets[deliveries](https://docs.omni.co/share/deliveries) support single tiles only.


See[Omni vs Sigma](https://www.basedash.com/vs/omni-vs-sigma) for a head-to-head.


## Row Zero: best for Excel users who need warehouse-scale data


**Best for:** finance, operations, and marketing analysts who live in Excel and want the same formulas, shortcuts, and cell-level control on billions of warehouse rows. **Not ideal for:** governed company dashboards, or teams that need a sub-daily scheduled refresh.


- **Pricing:** Free is $0 for one workbook. Pro is $12 and Business is $20 per user per month billed annually ($15 and $25 monthly), and Enterprise is custom ([Row Zero pricing](https://rowzero.com/pricing) ). Verified November 2026.
- **Acquisition:**[Databricks announced it acquired Row Zero](https://www.databricks.com/company/newsroom/press-releases/databricks-acquires-row-zero-bringing-live-governed-spreadsheets) on September 24, 2026. The release says Genie “will gain a native, fully-governed spreadsheet experience” and that Row Zero “will continue to feature support for data sources beyond Databricks.” As of November 19, Databricks release notes don’t list a Genie spreadsheet launch, and Row Zero still sells its own plans.
- **Spreadsheet features:** “400+ Excel-compatible functions,”[pivot tables](https://rowzero.com/docs/pivot-tables) , and typed cell inputs alongside live data. Workbooks hold 5 GB (10M+ rows) on Free, Pro, and Business; Enterprise lists “1 billion+ rows.” Write-back is on Business and Enterprise.
- **Query model:** a[connected table](https://rowzero.com/docs/data-import) “runs a query against a connection and imports the results into your workbook.” Results refresh on demand, and Business and Enterprise users can schedule refreshes. Connections cover Snowflake, Databricks, Redshift, Postgres, SQL Server, Oracle, Athena, S3, Teradata, and BigQuery (Enterprise only).
- **Security:** with[OAuth connections](https://rowzero.com/docs/databricks) , queries “respect the database permissions of the person who runs the query, including RLS and RBAC.” SAML or OIDC[SSO](https://rowzero.com/docs/singlesignon) and SCIM are Enterprise features. Row Zero is SOC 2 Type II certified ([Row Zero security](https://rowzero.com/security) ).
- **AI:** the[AI Agent](https://rowzero.com/docs/ai-assistant) turns plain-language questions into SQL using “the semantic layer configured in your data platform” (Snowflake Semantic Views or Databricks Genie spaces), then lands the result as a refreshable connected table.
- **Tradeoff:** Row Zero has no metric layer of its own, so consistency depends on the warehouse semantic layer, and its roadmap now sits inside Databricks.


## Microsoft Excel with Power BI semantic models: best for Microsoft 365 organizations


**Best for:** companies that already publish Power BI semantic models and want finance teams pivoting on governed measures in Excel. **Not ideal for:** teams without a Power BI developer, or anyone expecting Excel to query Snowflake directly.


- **Pricing:** Power BI Pro is $14 and Premium Per User is $24 per user per month, paid yearly ([Power BI pricing](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/products/power-bi/pricing) ). Copilot in Excel for enterprise plans needs the[Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/pricing/enterprise) at $30 per user per month, paid yearly. Verified November 2026.
- **How it works:** in Excel, choose Insert, PivotTable,[From Power BI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/collaborate-share/service-connect-excel-power-bi-datasets) to pivot on a published model’s tables and measures.[Analyze in Excel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/collaborate-share/service-analyze-in-excel) needs a Fabric Free, Pro, or PPU license, and export with live connection is capped at 500,000 rows.
- **Warehouse access:** the[Power Query connector index](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-query/connectors/) lists Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, and Redshift as unavailable in Excel, so Excel reaches them through a Power BI semantic model. Databricks also ships its own Excel add-in, with[scheduled refresh in Public Preview](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october) as of October 2026.
- **Security:** Microsoft states that “Row-level security (RLS) and object-level security (OLS) are supported for Analyze in Excel,” and the model’s sensitivity label carries into the workbook. Users outside your tenant can’t load Power BI data into Excel.
- **AI:**[Copilot in Excel](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/copilot/get-started-with-copilot-in-excel) shows insights “as charts, PivotTables, summaries, trends, or outliers.”
- **Tradeoff:** governance lives in Power BI Desktop and DAX, so every new metric waits for whoever maintains the model.


## Google Sheets Connected Sheets: best for BigQuery teams on Google Workspace


**Best for:** companies on BigQuery and Google Workspace that want analysts pivoting on full tables in Sheets, or on LookML fields through Looker. **Not ideal for:** Snowflake or Databricks shops without Looker.


- **Pricing:** Connected Sheets has no separate license; it needs “a project with billing setup in BigQuery,” so queries bill to your Google Cloud project ([Connected Sheets help](https://support.google.com/docs/answer/9702507) ). Verified November 2026.
- **Warehouses:**[BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/connected-sheets) natively and[Looker](https://cloud.google.com/looker/docs/connected-sheets) , which in turn connects to Snowflake, Redshift, and other databases.
- **Query model and limits:** Connected Sheets “runs BigQuery queries on your behalf either upon your request or on a defined schedule,” and saves results in the spreadsheet. Pivot tables return up to 200,000 rows, and[extracts](https://support.google.com/docs/answer/9703214) pull up to 500,000 rows.
- **Governed metrics:** Connected Sheets for Looker exposes “views, fields, and measures just as they were defined in Looker,” and Looker access filters still apply.
- **Security:**[admin docs](https://support.google.com/a/answer/9604541) say each user’s actions “depend on their IAM role and spreadsheet permissions, not the spreadsheet owner’s permissions,” and activity is recorded in Drive log events and Cloud Audit Logs.
- **AI:** since October 2026,[Gemini in Sheets](https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/10/analyze-bigquery-data-using-natural-language-with-Gemini-in-Google-Sheets.html) answers natural-language questions against the full BigQuery dataset on Business Standard and Plus and Enterprise Standard and Plus editions, running read-only queries.
- **Tradeoff:** Connected Sheets has no native connector for Snowflake, Databricks, or Postgres; those need Looker or another tool in between.


## Coefficient: best for keeping existing Sheets and Excel reports fed


**Best for:** teams that want to keep their current Google Sheets or Excel reports and replace copy-paste with scheduled warehouse imports. **Not ideal for:** governed self-serve analytics, or small teams on Snowflake or BigQuery who want a low-cost plan.


- **Pricing:** Free is $0 with 5,000-row imports and manual refresh. Starter is $49 per month and Pro is $99 per user per month (up to 5 users) billed annually, or $59 and $119 monthly. Enterprise is custom ([Coefficient pricing](https://coefficient.io/pricing) ). There’s a 30-day Pro trial. Verified November 2026.
- **Warehouse gating:** “Premium data sources include Snowflake, Tableau, Looker, BigQuery, Databricks, SQL Server, ClickHouse, NetSuite and Sage Intacct,” and only Enterprise includes premium sources. Postgres, MySQL, and Redshift are standard sources.
- **Query model:** Coefficient runs a query at import time and lands the result in the sheet; it says imports “are never stored on our servers” ([data security](https://help.coefficient.io/hc/en-us/articles/17575143684123-Data-Security) ).[Refreshes](https://help.coefficient.io/hc/en-us/articles/17227106438171-Import-Refreshes) run every 1, 2, 4, or 8 hours, daily, or weekly.
- **Write-back and metrics:** exports can write rows back to Snowflake, BigQuery, and SQL databases, and imports can come from Snowflake Semantic Views and Looker.
- **Security:**[Snowflake OAuth](https://help.coefficient.io/hc/en-us/articles/18180164081947-Snowflake) lets users sign in with their own Snowflake logins, but shared connections query with the owner’s credentials. SSO is OIDC on Enterprise, and the[admin console](https://help.coefficient.io/hc/en-us/articles/22560802749595-Admin) keeps 30 days of run history.
- **Tradeoff:** Coefficient is a connector, not a BI layer. Each spreadsheet still holds its own formulas, so metric drift between sheets is up to you.


## Quadratic: best for analysts who mix formulas with Python and SQL


**Best for:** technical analysts and small data teams who want SQL, Python, and formulas in one grid, with an option to self-host. **Not ideal for:** per-user warehouse permissions or Databricks and Redshift users.


- **Pricing:** Personal is free. Pro is $18 and Business is $36 per user per month billed annually ($20 and $40 monthly), with $20 and $40 of monthly AI credits; Enterprise is custom ([Quadratic pricing](https://www.quadratichq.com/pricing) ). Verified November 2026.
- **Warehouses:**[SQL connections](https://docs.quadratichq.com/connections/sql-getting-started) cover PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery, CockroachDB, MariaDB, Supabase, and Neon. Databricks and Redshift connector pages say the connectors are still in development.
- **Query model:** SQL results are returned to the sheet, and scheduled tasks “can run at most once per hour.” Quadratic can also write to connected databases.
- **Security:** connections allow “all the queries and table access granted by the database user credentials” ([connection security](https://docs.quadratichq.com/connections/security) ), so everyone using a connection shares its access. SSO is an Enterprise feature, and[self-hosting](https://docs.quadratichq.com/self-hosting/getting-started) is offered on Business and Enterprise.
- **AI:** AI chat writes SQL, Python, and formulas, and a hosted MCP server lets outside assistants read and write sheets.
- **Tradeoff:** no semantic layer; each connection stores AI context notes, but metric definitions live in individual files.


## Equals: best for go-to-market teams that want analysis done for them


**Best for:** revenue, sales, and marketing teams that want spreadsheet-style reports on CRM and billing data, built initially by Equals’ own analysts. **Not ideal for:** small teams, Databricks users, or companies that want self-serve setup.


- **Pricing:** flat annual pricing with unlimited seats: Essential $24,000, Business $36,000, and Enterprise $60,000 per year, each with included AI spend ([Equals pricing](https://equals.com/pricing) ). There is no free tier. Verified November 2026.
- **Warehouses:** connecting your own warehouse (BigQuery, ClickHouse, Dremio, Redshift, or Snowflake) starts on Business. SaaS sources sync through Fivetran into a Snowflake instance Equals runs, every 6 hours on Essential down to every 15 minutes on Enterprise.
- **Spreadsheet features:**[pivot tables](https://docs.equals.com/docs/pivot-tables) on query results, manual edits that persist across refreshes, and write-back to HubSpot and Salesforce.
- **Governed metrics:** workbooks can be approved as “a canonical source of truth for your team.”
- **Security:** a shared data source lets others query it “as if they were the user who set it up” ([sharing permissions](https://docs.equals.com/docs/sharing-permissions) ). Enterprise SSO is listed, and Equals is SOC 2 Type II certified.
- **Tradeoff:** the entry price is high for a spreadsheet on the warehouse.


## Basedash: best for ops teams that would rather ask than build formulas


**Best for:** startups and mid-size companies whose operations and finance people want answers and dashboards from warehouse data without writing SQL or formulas. **Not ideal for:** anyone who needs a real spreadsheet with formulas, cell inputs, or write-back, or a free tier.


- **Pricing:** Startup is $1,000 per month plus AI usage for up to 25 users, including $1,000 per month in AI credits; Enterprise is custom ([Basedash pricing](https://www.basedash.com/pricing) ). 14-day free trial, no card. Verified November 2026.
- **Spreadsheet-like features:** the[table view](https://www.basedash.com/docs/features/tables) gives a spreadsheet-like grid with search, filters, multi-column sort, and pinned columns on live data, but tables are read-only and don’t support formulas. Chart and table data[exports to Excel](https://www.basedash.com/docs/features/export-and-share) up to 1,000,000 rows, and chat accepts uploaded Excel and CSV files up to 50 MB.
- **AI:** the[AI data analyst](https://www.basedash.com/features/ai-data-analyst) answers questions in chat, shows the SQL it ran, and builds charts and[dashboards](https://www.basedash.com/features/dashboards) . An MCP server is included on every plan.
- **Governed metrics:**[models](https://www.basedash.com/features/models) define SQL, measures, and segments that the AI reuses, with version history and admin verification.
- **Security and audit:**[row-level security](https://www.basedash.com/docs/administration/row-level-security) works on Postgres and Supabase only; on Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks,[data source access control](https://www.basedash.com/docs/administration/data-source-access-control) limits schemas, tables, and columns per group. SSO, SCIM, and[audit logs](https://www.basedash.com/docs/administration/audit-logs) that record queries, exports, and AI tool calls are Enterprise features.
- **Tradeoff:** Basedash replaces the spreadsheet step with chat rather than putting a grid on the warehouse. Teams whose work depends on hand-built formulas should pick Row Zero, Sigma, or Omni.


## Which spreadsheet-style BI tool should you choose?


**Operations teams need spreadsheet exploration with consistent KPIs across departments.** Sigma (data models and metrics) and Omni (shared semantic model with dbt) are the two tools where the grid sits directly on governed definitions. Excel on Power BI semantic models does the same for Microsoft shops. Our[comparison of BI tools with built-in semantic layers](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-bi-tools-with-built-in-semantic-layers-compared-2026) covers how those definitions are maintained.


**Leadership needs audit logs and lineage while ops works ad hoc.** Sigma, Omni, Google Workspace, and Basedash Enterprise record audit logs, and Sigma, Omni, and Power BI keep metric logic in a shared model instead of individual sheets. Row Zero, Quadratic, and Coefficient leave logic inside individual workbooks.


**Your finance team lives in Excel.** Row Zero gives Excel formulas and cell inputs on warehouse data. If your company already runs Power BI, Excel PivotTables on its semantic models are the lowest-change option. Our[guide to BI tools for finance teams](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-bi-tools-for-finance-teams-compared-2026) covers variance reporting and ERP connectors.


**You’re on Snowflake and business users must work without SQL.** Sigma and Omni query Snowflake live; Row Zero imports Snowflake results into a refreshable sheet. Coefficient requires its Enterprise plan for Snowflake.


**You’re on BigQuery and Google Workspace.** Connected Sheets is included, and Gemini in Sheets now answers questions against the full table.


**You want to keep existing spreadsheets.** Coefficient refreshes current Sheets and Excel files on a schedule. If you’re ready to move reporting out of spreadsheets entirely, see our[guide to tools that replace Excel dashboards](https://www.basedash.com/blog/best-tools-to-replace-excel-dashboards-in-2026) .


**Your team would rather ask questions than build pivots.** Basedash is built around chat first; Omni Agent, Sigma Assistant, and Gemini in Sheets add chat to a grid.


## Frequently asked questions


### Which BI tools let operations teams explore data like spreadsheets while keeping KPIs consistent?


Sigma and Omni are the main options as of November 2026. Sigma’s workbooks look and behave like a spreadsheet on live warehouse data, and its data models and metrics give everyone the same definitions. Omni’s spreadsheet tabs use Excel-style formulas on top of a shared semantic model that can sync with dbt. Microsoft Excel connected to Power BI semantic models offers the same pattern for Microsoft 365 companies, with measures defined once in Power BI and pivoted in Excel.


### Is Sigma Computing a real spreadsheet?


Not in the Excel sense. Sigma is a BI platform with a spreadsheet-style interface: you work with tables, pivots, and 200+ functions on live warehouse data, but functions calculate over columns and groups rather than individual cell references. Typed values go into input tables, which write to your warehouse. Teams that need cell-by-cell Excel models usually look at Row Zero, which supports more than 400 Excel-compatible functions, or keep Excel connected to a governed model.


### What happened to Row Zero after Databricks acquired it?


Databricks announced the acquisition on September 24, 2026, and said Genie will gain a native, governed spreadsheet experience built on Row Zero, and that Row Zero will keep supporting data sources beyond Databricks. As of November 19, 2026, the Genie spreadsheet hasn’t appeared in Databricks release notes, and Row Zero still sells Free, Pro ($12 per user per month billed annually), Business ($20), and Enterprise plans on its own site.


### Can Excel connect directly to Snowflake or BigQuery?


Not through Power Query. Microsoft’s connector index lists Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, and Redshift as unavailable in Excel, while Postgres, MySQL, and SQL Server work. The usual route is a Power BI semantic model that connects to the warehouse, which Excel users then pivot through Analyze in Excel with RLS applied. Third-party add-ins such as Coefficient (Enterprise plan for Snowflake and BigQuery) and the Databricks Excel add-in also pull warehouse data into Excel.


### Do spreadsheet BI tools query the warehouse live or copy the data?


It varies. Sigma and Basedash query the warehouse on each interaction, and Omni queries live with a 6-hour default cache. Row Zero, Coefficient, Quadratic, and Google Connected Sheets store query results in the sheet and refresh them on demand or on a schedule, which is cheaper on the warehouse but only as current as the last refresh.


### Which spreadsheet-style tools respect warehouse row-level security for each user?


Tools that connect as each user can pass warehouse policies through. Row Zero OAuth connections “respect the database permissions of the person who runs the query,” Connected Sheets uses each user’s BigQuery IAM role, and Coefficient supports per-user Snowflake OAuth. Sigma and Omni apply their own row-level rules by user attribute, and Power BI’s RLS carries into Excel. Quadratic and Equals connections run with shared credentials, so everyone sees what that login can see.


### What’s the cheapest way to give a team spreadsheet access to warehouse data?


On BigQuery and Google Workspace, Connected Sheets has no extra license beyond BigQuery query costs. Row Zero’s Pro plan is $12 per user per month billed annually, and Quadratic’s Pro plan is $18, both as of November 2026. Coefficient’s Starter plan is $49 per month but doesn’t include Snowflake or BigQuery. Sigma and Omni are quote-only, and Equals starts at $24,000 per year.
